s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of fever, skin lesions, and chest pain with cardiac involvement
salient_findings: Sudden appearance of skin lesions at the base of the penis
Development of fever, chest pain, and shortness of breath
Vesicular and umbilicated lesions on genitals with lymphadenomegaly
key_facts: 42-year-old man with a 12-year history of well-controlled HIV
Past medical history includes treatment for early latent syphilis
Recent sexual activity with multiple male partners
Low-grade fever (37.5°) at presentation
Fever up to 39°C two days after initial skin manifestations
Chest pain without irradiation and shortness of breath
Hemodynamically stable with continuous anterior chest pain
High-sensitivity cardiac troponin elevated at 128.00 pg/ml
ECG showed sinus tachycardia with elevated PR segment in aVR lead
Echocardiography showed left ventricle diastolic diameter of 59 mm and EF 50%
Cardiac MRI showed slightly increased global T1 and T2 mapping values
Episodes of sinus pauses, advanced AV block, and sinus bradycardia

shortlist.label: Myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated cardiac troponin and echocardiography showing left ventricle diastolic diameter of 59 mm with EF 50%

shortlist.label: Acute pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Cardiac MRI showing slightly increased global T1 and T2 mapping values and minimal hyperintensity of pericardium

shortlist.label: Syphilitic coronary arteritis
shortlist.why_kept: Past medical history of treated syphilis and recent sexual activity with multiple partners

shortlist.label: Disseminated herpes simplex virus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Skin lesions and fever, although viral serologies were negative

shortlist.label: Human immunodeficiency virus-associated cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: 12-year history of well-controlled HIV and cardiac symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with chest pain, shortness of breath, and elevated high-sensitivity cardiac troponin levels, along with echocardiography and cardiac MRI findings, is consistent with myocarditis. The recent onset of fever and skin lesions, followed by cardiac symptoms, also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Acute pericarditis
rejected.why: The cardiac MRI showed minimal hyperintensity of pericardium without effusion, which is not typical for acute pericarditis

rejected.label: Syphilitic coronary arteritis
rejected.why: The patient's past medical history of treated syphilis and the lack of evidence for coronary artery involvement on coronary CT angiography make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Disseminated herpes simplex virus infection
rejected.why: The patient's viral serologies, including Herpes virus 1/2, were negative, making this diagnosis unlikely

rejected.label: Human immunodeficiency virus-associated cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The patient's well-controlled HIV status and the acute onset of symptoms make this diagnosis less likely
